scenes.title: Colombo Street collapse

briefing.exactLocation: Colombo Street and Hereford Street, Christchurch CBD
briefing.type: Earthquake, two shop fronts and part of a car park building collapsed
briefing.hazards: Aftershocks, cracking walls, falling glass, possible gas leak
briefing.access: From Colombo Street, north side, through the cordon
briefing.number: About 10 casualties, more may be inside
briefing.emergencyServices: Fire and Emergency NZ urban search and rescue 20 minutes out. Hato Hone St John staging at Latimer Square, 10 minutes out

override.approach: Man lying still on his back at the edge of the footpath behind a toppled planter box, eyes closed, with a cut on his head and bruising on his face.
override.mechanism: Struck by falling masonry from a shop front when the earthquake hit. A passer-by saw him go down and he has not spoken since.

bystanders.description: Man in a work shirt and lanyard, calm and steady
lines: I did a first aid course last year. Tell me what to do.
I've got it. I'll keep pressing.

bystanders.description: Woman in a green coat, gripping her phone
lines: Fatima first, please! She's only stuck under a shelf!
Can't you just lift it off her?

bystanders.description: Young man in a hoodie holding up his phone
lines: This is crazy, I'm live-streaming this.
Can you say something to the camera?

events.description: Control: urban search and rescue is about 20 minutes away. Keep walking casualties together away from the buildings.
The woman in the green coat grabs your sleeve and demands you free her friend Fatima first.
A strong aftershock. The shop wall above the footpath cracks and dust pours down.
A strong smell of gas drifts across the footpath. Fire and Emergency NZ calls for everyone to move back.

teaching: Call out for walking wounded first so the green casualties leave the building area, then sieve the people left behind.
Look at everyone before you commit. The quiet man behind the planter is easy to miss, and he is red.
Not breathing after one airway opening is black. Do not start CPR while red and orange casualties wait.
When the ground shakes, drop, cover and hold, then withdraw. When you smell gas, withdraw first and go back when the danger has passed.
Flag trapped casualties for medical and leave lifting to the rescue crews. A friend demanding a release does not change the order.
A wheelchair user who is not hurt still cannot join the walking wounded. Ask how he wants to be moved and keep his chair with him.

scenes.title: Lindis Pass coach crash

briefing.exactLocation: State Highway 8, Lindis Pass, Central Otago
briefing.type: Coach carrying tourists and a school sports group swerved off the road, hit a bank and rolled onto its side. A car it swerved to avoid also overturned
briefing.hazards: Passing traffic, smoke from the engine bay, steep bank
briefing.access: From the Tarras side. Park well back and walk in along the verge
briefing.number: About 35 on board plus the car occupants, at least 9 injured
briefing.emergencyServices: Fire and Emergency NZ from Omarama and Hato Hone St John from Cromwell, 30 minutes out. Rescue helicopter requested

override.approach: Elderly man sitting on the gravel verge beside the overturned coach, restless and anxious, holding his head where there is a small cut with a little bleeding, his left lower leg bent at an odd angle.
override.mechanism: Thrown from his seat when the coach rolled. He hit his head and twisted his left ankle.

override.approach: Man sitting on the gravel verge beside the overturned coach, shouting and moving about, holding his left forearm, which is visibly bent.
override.mechanism: Thrown across the aisle when the coach rolled, landing on his left arm.

override.approach: Man sitting on the road verge near the overturned coach, calm, saying he is fine, with a graze on his left forearm.

override.mechanism: Passenger on a tour coach that swerved off the state highway and hit a bank. He was wearing a seatbelt and was jolted against it.

override.approach: Girl in a school uniform sitting on the grass bank beside the road, crying and calling for her mum, with a scraped right shin.
override.mechanism: Scraped her shin climbing out of the coach through an emergency window. She lost her mum in the confusion on the roadside.

bystanders.description: Truck driver in a hi-vis top who stopped to help
lines: I'm a truckie, I stopped when I saw it. What do you need?
Tell me where to press and I'll hold it.

bystanders.description: Older woman in a green cardigan, Eru's wife
lines: Eru first, please! He's hurt his head!
You can't just walk past him!

bystanders.description: Woman in a fleece searching along the verge
lines: Aroha? Has anyone seen my daughter, Aroha?
She's six, in a school uniform.

events.description: Control: crews are 30 minutes out and the helicopter is on its way. Keep a clear landing area on the flat paddock below the road.
Mere grabs your arm and insists you stay with her husband Eru.
Thick smoke starts pouring from the engine bay at the front of the coach.
The first Fire and Emergency NZ appliance arrives from Omarama and the crew starts to extinguish the engine bay.

teaching: A pale, sweaty passenger with no visible blood needs expose and look. A hidden bleed under a jacket needs a tourniquet in seconds.
Use your bystanders. The truck driver can hold pressure while you carry on, and a parent can give a child's name and history.
A worried relative pulling you to one casualty does not change the order. Sieve everyone and come back.
Smoke from the engine bay means withdraw. Go back when the crew says it is safe.
Trapped, breathing fast, blue-grey lips: red. Flag for medical and do not try to cut him out yourself.
The woman thrown from the car is not breathing after one airway opening: black. Tag her and keep moving.

scenes.title: Grandstand collapse

briefing.exactLocation: Community rugby ground, Hastings, Hawke's Bay
briefing.type: Earthquake, temporary grandstand partly collapsed during a school sports and rugby day
briefing.hazards: Aftershocks, unstable terraces, loose seating overhead
briefing.access: Through the gate off the car park, then across the field
briefing.number: About 10 casualties here, more reported near the exit
briefing.emergencyServices: Hato Hone St John event medics on site. Fire and Emergency NZ and ambulances 10 minutes out

override.approach: Woman sitting upright on the terracing with her right arm pinned under a fallen steel beam from the stand roof, dusty, looking frightened.
override.mechanism: Part of the stand roof came down and a beam fell across her right arm about ten minutes ago.

override.approach: Toddler sitting on the concrete among broken seats, dusty and crying.
override.mechanism: Seating fell onto the lower rows when the stand collapsed. His dad saw him sit up and cry straight away.

override.approach: Woman sitting in her wheelchair at the edge of the field, calm, with grazes on both palms, saying she can get herself to the point.
override.mechanism: Was in the accessible seating at the front of the stand when it collapsed. She wheeled herself clear across the gravel and grazed both palms on the wheels.

override.approach: Woman standing, dusted grey with concrete dust, a pink burn mark on her right forearm, looking distressed and saying she cannot stop coughing.
override.mechanism: Caught in the dust cloud when the stand came down. She was scalded on the forearm by a spilled hot water urn from the canteen behind the stand.
teaching: A casualty who can walk is green in the first sweep, even with a cough and a small burn.
Dust irritates the airways for a while: her rate of 28 to 30 is close to the cut-off, so count it again at re-triage.
If she can no longer walk and breathes faster than 30, she is red.
Ask about asthma and medicines at re-triage, not in the first sweep.

bystanders.description: Man in a club jersey holding a baby bag
lines: That's Ethan, he's one. He was on my knee and then everything came down.
He just sat up and started crying.

bystanders.description: Woman in a first aid vest who was spectating, calm
lines: I'm a first aider. Tell me what you want me to do.
I'll keep the pressure on.

bystanders.description: Teenage boy holding up a phone
lines: Did you see that? It just came down!
Can you tell the camera what's happening?

events.description: Hato Hone St John event medics arrive from the first aid post and offer to take the green casualties to the centre of the field.
The boy with the sore wrist cries out again, loudly: 'My wrist! I want Mum!'
An aftershock. The remaining rows of the stand creak and the upper terrace sags above you.
Control: the rescue helicopter lands in 10 minutes on the far side of the field. Keep that area clear.

teaching: Two catastrophic bleeds, one on an adult and one on a child: stop each one before anything else, then tag red.
Use the child sieve for all three children. A child who can walk is green even when crying. A child who cannot walk because of age cannot be cleared as green.
Crying and shouting are not signs of serious injury. Hand the green casualties to the helpers and move on.
A wheelchair user who can reach the walking-wounded point is green. Ask what she can do rather than telling her to stand.
When the terrace sags, drop, cover and hold, then withdraw. Go back when the danger is cleared.

scenes.title: Riverbank Road flood

briefing.exactLocation: Riverbank Road, Edgecumbe, Bay of Plenty
briefing.type: River flood, stopbank breached, street being evacuated to the school hall on high ground
briefing.hazards: Rising water, fast current, floating debris
briefing.access: On foot along the raised road from the school hall end. Stay out of the water
briefing.number: About 9 casualties here, more being brought out by boat
briefing.emergencyServices: Fire and Emergency NZ swift-water rescue 20 minutes out. Hato Hone St John 15 minutes out. Police and Civil Defence setting up at the school hall

override.mechanism: Pulled from the flood water by neighbours after the river swept through his street. He was under for several minutes.
Fast flood water swept debris down the street. A timber beam fell across his left leg and he landed face down.
A surge of flood water ran up the street when the stopbank gave way. She was knocked off her feet and scrambled out unhurt.
Ran for higher ground and was knocked over by a surge of flood water, landing on his right side against a fence post.
teaching: He walks and talks, so he is green in the first sweep, even though the current knocked him down hard.
Chest injuries can declare themselves late: fast, shallow breathing and a struggle to stand mean red.
Re-triage walking casualties who took a hard blow to the chest or belly, and expose the area to look for bruising.

bystanders.description: Man in a wet hoodie who pulled the child out of the water
lines: I pulled her out of the water. She wasn't breathing.
What can I do? Tell me and I'll do it.

bystanders.description: Man in soaked work clothes searching along the road
lines: Mele? Has anyone seen Mele? She's four!
She was right beside me when the water came.

bystanders.description: Man on the stopbank filming the water on his phone
lines: Look at that current! Nobody will believe this.
Hey, come and look at this!

events.description: Control: the stopbank has breached upstream and the river is still rising. Swift-water crews are about 20 minutes away.
The man on the stopbank calls you over to film the water surging down the street.
Water surges over the road at the low end of the street and rises quickly toward the casualties.
A Fire and Emergency NZ swift-water crew arrives by boat at the school hall end and starts bringing more people out.

teaching: Most casualties walk out of a flood. Call out for the walking wounded first, then sieve the people left behind.
A child who is not breathing but has a pulse gets five rescue breaths after the airway is opened. If she is still not breathing, or has no pulse, she is black.
Count the breaths on the near-drowned man: more than 30 a minute is red, even though he is awake and talking.
A casualty who cannot get up is orange even when nothing looks broken. Ask a walking casualty or a helper to bring a blanket.
When the water starts rising over the road, withdraw to high ground. Do not go back for the trapped man until the swift-water crew says it is safe.
